answer: An agent economy can slow Sybil creation with a sequential onboarding puzzle that cannot be split across machines. Each new identity must solve a verifiable delay function, turning registration into a long, steady pulse of computation rather than a cheap instant copy. Like mapping an atlas before crossing an ocean, the delay is checked quickly by others, but generating a thousand fake identities would require a thousand sequential waits. Honest agents pay this cost once, while an attacker faces linear wall-clock time, making mass forgery expensive and easy to spot.
